answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using proof-of-spacetime, requiring identities to persistently store designated public data, such as radar surveys of an arctic tundra or spectral scans of an opal mine. Validators periodically query nodes to verify data presence via a symmetric cipher, forcing adversaries to commit scarce non-volatile storage hardware and bandwidth per replica. A primary limitation is that these heavy storage demands disadvantage lightweight, low-footprint agents.
